title: Traveling first class with Louis; his bad heart
summary: Armstrong's tours were hard but first class; he had heart trouble and a heart attack at Spoleto.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: How about traveling with Louis Armstrong? That was much later in comparison with the big band travel we were talking about before, but Louis always went first class.

He did, but it was hard. I'll tell you something about one-nighters. I don't care how you do them, they're hard. But at least it was first class, the way we traveled with Louis. It was -- it was rough, but it was first class.
You had nights off sometimes, didn't you? It seems to me I used to see the --

When I first went with Louis, we didn't have many nights off because he was strong then, you know, and he was very strong. And he played hard, and he didn't want to relax. But later on as he got a little weaker, then we started having nights off. See, Louis had a case history of a
bad heart for a long time.

Well, at least 20 years. Yeah. I know we did a thing over in Spoleto, Italy, you know, and he had a pretty bad heart attack over there. He had to take off. We did an Ed Sullivan thing over there. And he had to take off. That Carlos Menotti thing, you know, he did over there one year, and he had to -- he had to take off for about two, three weeks, and what -- he came back soon as it was, about three weeks after a heart attack like that.

They -- Ed Sullivan was crying. He didn't think he would make it. But Louis was strong. Louis was perhaps the strongest guy I ever worked around, because he -- he didn't -- you know, he didn't try to live carefully or anything like this. He lived the way he wanted to live, and the heck with it. That's how he lived, you know?
